name: Mental Maths: Multiplication Foundations — Tables, Anchors & Transformations
description: A KaTeX-enabled mental-arithmetic deck that develops multiplication fluency through high-value table anchors, extension facts through 20, reverse fact families, doubling and halving, special multipliers, factor pairing, estimation, error detection, and method selection. It teaches students when a transformation is genuinely useful rather than presenting tricks as universal.
estimatedTime: 150–190 minutes for the first pass; then 10–15 minute review bursts

cards.term: Multiplication Foundations: What is the mental-maths goal?
cards.definition:
The goal is not to memorise a random trick for every question. Spot structure:

• a known table fact
• a friendly factor such as 2, 4, 5, 25, 50, or 125
• a nearby base such as 10, 20, 50, or 100
• an opportunity to double one factor and halve the other

Choose the route with the lowest cognitive load.

cards.term: Multiplication Foundations: What does factor transformation mean?
cards.definition:
You may change factors while preserving the product.

$$
\begin{aligned}
16\times25 \\
&=8\times50 \\
&=4\times100 \\
&=400
\end{aligned}
$$
One factor is halved while the other is doubled, so the product stays unchanged.

cards.term: Multiplication Foundations: What is the distributive property?
cards.definition:
Split a factor into easier parts.

$$
\begin{aligned}
47\times6 \\
&=(40+7)\times6 \\
&=40\times6+7\times6 \\
&=240+42 \\
&=282
\end{aligned}
$$
This is the reliable default when no faster special pattern appears.

cards.term: Multiplication Foundations: When should you use doubling and halving?
cards.definition:
Use it when halving one factor stays exact and doubling the other creates a friendly number.

$$
\begin{aligned}
24\times125 \\
&=12\times250 \\
&=6\times500 \\
&=3\times1000 \\
&=3000
\end{aligned}
$$
It is especially useful around 25, 50, 125, 250, and 500.

cards.term: Multiplication Foundations: Why are 25, 50, and 125 powerful?
cards.definition:
They connect directly to powers of 10:

$$
\begin{aligned}
25\times4&=100 \\
50\times2&=100 \\
125\times8&=1000
\end{aligned}
$$
Look for factors of 4, 2, or 8 that can pair with them.

cards.term: Multiplication Foundations: How do you multiply by 9 mentally?
cards.definition:
Use 9 = 10 − 1.

$$
\begin{aligned}
47\times9 \\
&=47\times(10-1) \\
&=470-47 \\
&=423
\end{aligned}
$$
This is usually easier than repeated addition.

cards.term: Multiplication Foundations: How do you multiply by 11 mentally?
cards.definition:
Use 11 = 10 + 1.

$$
\begin{aligned}
36\times11 \\
&=36\times(10+1) \\
&=360+36 \\
&=396
\end{aligned}
$$
A more advanced digit-insertion method comes later; this is the dependable foundation.

cards.term: Multiplication Foundations: How do you multiply by 19 mentally?
cards.definition:
Use 19 = 20 − 1.

$$
\begin{aligned}
34\times19 \\
&=34\times20-34 \\
&=680-34 \\
&=646
\end{aligned}
$$
This is strong when multiplying by 20 is effortless.

cards.term: Multiplication Foundations: What is a good estimate for a product?
cards.definition:
Round to friendly values before calculating exactly.

Example:
47 × 18 ≈ 50 × 20 = 1000

The exact answer should be in the same general region. Estimation catches large errors; it does not replace exact calculation.

cards.term: Multiplication Foundations: When should you not force a shortcut?
cards.definition:
Do not use a transformation if it adds more steps than direct splitting.

For example:
$$
\begin{aligned}
43\times6 \\
&=40\times6+3\times6 \\
&=240+18 \\
&=258
\end{aligned}
$$
This is cleaner than inventing an unnecessary special method.

cards.term: Multiplication Foundations: How can you self-check a product?
cards.definition:
Use at least one quick check:

• Estimate the size.
• Check the last digit.
• Reverse with division when convenient.

Example: 48 × 25 must end in 00 because 25 × 4 = 100 and 48 contains a factor of 4.

cards.term: Multiplication Foundations: What does commutativity allow?
cards.definition:
You may reverse the order of factors:

$$
\begin{aligned}
16\times75&=75\times16 \\
7\times48&=48\times7
\end{aligned}
$$
Reorder factors so the friendlier multiplier is easier to use.
